title: Cohort-driven KV lifecycle: hybrid LRU/TTL with batch-consistent eviction
creator: Leah Kim
description:
Problem: Under continuous batching workloads we observe bursty prefix activity that causes traditional global LRU eviction to thrash small, hot prefixes (increasing end-to-end latency and causing incorrect KV lookups when a partitioned shard evicts entries mid-request). Goal: design a correctness-first eviction policy that is GPU-memory efficient and plays well with the continuous batching pipeline and multi-tenant routing.

Proposal: introduce a cohort-driven hybrid policy that combines short-lived cohort TTLs, per-cohort local LRU lists, and prefix-aware pinning for active generation windows. Key ideas: 1) Segment the KV namespace into cohorts based on recent batch affinity (e.g., request origin + model-version + route-hash) to limit LRU churn across unrelated workloads. 2) Apply two-tier TTL: a soft TTL that makes keys eligible for background compaction and a hard TTL enforced before eviction reclamation. 3) During an active batch window (request in flight or reserved KV-cache for a session), entries are pinned via a batch-consistent lock to prevent mid-request eviction. 4) Eviction is performed atomically at cohort level: compaction snapshots are computed off the hot path, then a single CAS-like commit removes entries and updates GPU allocation metadata to avoid dangling pointers.

Correctness guarantees to assert: 1) No prefix/pair used by an in-flight generation is reclaimed until the generation completes or is aborted. 2) After eviction commit, subsequent requests must either miss cleanly (and trigger a reload) or be routed to compatible fallback model variant; stale reads are impossible. 3) Memory accounting remains monotonic during eviction commit (no double-free, no leaked allocations). 4) Cohort isolation: eviction in one cohort cannot force eviction of live entries in another cohort except under explicit global OOM conditions.

Acceptance criteria: 1) End-to-end CI and integration tests proving no generation observes a missing KV pointer during controlled eviction scenarios (see test matrix). 2) Benchmarks: under realistic continuous-batching trace, tail latency improves or remains stable versus baseline while GPU memory reclaim improves by >= 12% for mixed workloads. 3) Chaos test: concurrent evictions + node handoff yields zero corrupted outputs in 50k simulated generations.
implementation_plan: Prototype: in-memory cohort LRU with simulated TTL (ENG branch: github.com/redwood/runtime/tree/eng/ENG-14321-cohort-proto)
Instrumentation: add cohort-id to trace/span and include cohort evict counters in console (runtime-1.21 target)
Eviction commit: implement off-path compaction with atomic GPU metadata swap, ship feature-flagged behind 'cohort-eviction'
Compatibility: add fallback routing policy to route to quantized model variant when eviction causes miss during warmup
Tests: unit tests for cohort isolation + integration tests with continuous batching harness, plus chaos script to simulate mid-request eviction
Rollout: canary on dedicated pool -> widen to 10% hosted -> full release, monitor per-route correctness metrics
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff. Drafted design doc and identified core invariants. Linked to ENG-5824 for historical eviction constraints.
2026-02-22: Spike completed: prototype shows cohort segmentation reduces LRU churn by ~30% on synthetic chat trace. Branch: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2416 (WIP)

2026-03-01: Design review with infra and runtime teams. Decision: prefer short soft TTL (5s) + hard TTL (60s) instead of purely LRU to bound memory pressure under bursts. Action: add additional metrics for soft/hard TTL expirations.
2026-03-05: Security review triage: no new surface for secret leakage; KMS/HSM unaffected. Flagged non-blocking. (sec ticket: SEC-993)
2026-03-08: Implemented pinning API for active batch windows. Integration tests show no mid-request evictions in local cluster run with 10k simulated concurrent generations.
2026-03-10: Opened PR for atomic eviction commit and GPU allocator metadata swap. Need review from @maria and @devops for allocator correctness. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2479
test_plan: Unit tests: cohort LRU ops, TTL transitions, and pin/unpin paths (mock allocator)
Integration: continuous-batching trace replay comparing baseline vs. cohort-policy (latency and memory metrics)
Chaos: simultaneous eviction + node drain + batch handoff, assert no corrupted outputs - 50k iterations
Fuzz: randomized cohort memberships and TTL jitter to catch ordering races
Performance: GPU memory reclaimed vs baseline, token-per-second throughput under target batch sizes
risks: Complexity: cohort segmentation increases metadata overhead per key; mitigate by compacting cohort ids and sampling for cold keys
Starvation: long-lived pinned cohorts could starve other tenants under sustained load; mitigation: global admission controller and emergency reclaim policy under OOM
Correctness: race between compaction snapshot and live batch pinning; mitigation: test harness with memory fences and atomic commit path
Observability: new metrics required to diagnose mis-evictions; add per-cohort eviction counters and allocation histograms
notes_and_links: Related tickets: ENG-5824 (prefix eviction guarantees), ENG-12673 (eviction emulator), ENG-9407 (adaptive prefix pinning)
